models.name: EXD-Knee v1.2 (Explicit Dynamics Articular Contact Model)
models.what_it_computes: Transient contact mechanics during gait and non-gait maneuvers using explicit time integration; outputs include contact pressure/area, shear traction, cross-shear index, subsurface stress in UHMWPE, and instantaneous post–cam impact loads.

models.name: EXD-WearGrow v2.0 (Adaptive Wear–Creep Growth Model)
models.what_it_computes: Cycle-by-cycle cumulative wear depth with surface evolution using explicit dynamics with adaptive remeshing; outputs include volumetric wear, directional wear maps, creep-induced deformation, and edge-loading progression under malalignment.

mechanisms.name: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines long-term UHMWPE volume loss and surface topography that drive revision risk.

mechanisms.name: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Controls risk of subsurface yielding and accelerated fatigue wear during kneeling or high-flexion activities.

mechanisms.name: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Concentrates load at the insert rim, elevating delamination and wear at the periphery.

mechanisms.name: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sets post stress and cam wear drivers that affect stability and debris generation in posterior-stabilized designs.

deviation.detail: Credibility scores are reported on a 0–12 scale with anchors at 3 (initially acceptable), 6 (adequate for comparative assessment), 9 (strong), and 12 (compelling).

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: The experimental datasets used to anchor inputs and check results were drawn primarily from dedicated instrumentedrig campaigns with traceable calibration and complete raw wave-forms accounting for 82% of all comparisons; the remainder came from peerreviewed simulator studies with full procedural reporting and sufficient metadata to reconstruct loads and kinematics.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: EXDKnee v1.2 emphasizes highfidelity transient contact and stress fields using explicit time integration.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: Energy balance checks tracked kinetic, internal, hourglass, contact, and artificial energies; cumulative artificial energy remained below 0.5% of the sum of kinetic and internal energies during level walking, 0.9% during deep flexion, 1.1% during rim loading, and 0.8% during post–cam impacts.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: For level walking, refining the articular inplane mesh from 0.5 to 0.35 mm and halving the time step changed EXDKnee v1.2 midstance peak pressure by 1.6% and contact area by 2.3%; EXDWearGrow v2.0’s 5 Mc wear volume changed by 3.8%.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: For EXDKnee v1.2, the 95% interval for midstance peak contact pressure was ±10.2% around 19.6 MPa, and the crossshear index distribution had a 95% halfwidth of 0.015 around 0.15.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: The simulator executed ISO 142431/3 gait cycles at 1 Hz using bovine serum (25 g/L protein) maintained at 37 ± 1 °C with viscosity checks at the start and end of each run (1.4 ± 0.1 mPa·s at 37 °C).

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: Pressure film (Fuji Prescale Super Low and Medium) was employed in deep flexion to map peak contact; films were preconditioned and calibrated per manufacturer instructions and digitized at 600 dpi with a 10bit scanner; a conversion curve was generated by platen compression (R2 = 0.997).

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: EXDKnee v1.2 emphasizes highfidelity transient contact and stress fields using explicit time integration.

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: Energy balance checks tracked kinetic, internal, hourglass, contact, and artificial energies; cumulative artificial energy remained below 0.5% of the sum of kinetic and internal energies during level walking, 0.9% during deep flexion, 1.1% during rim loading, and 0.8% during post–cam impacts.

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: EXDKnee v1.2 predicted peak contact pressure of 32.4 ± 2.5 MPa versus filmderived 35.0 ± 3.3 MPa (7.4%), with a posteriorized footprint shift of 2.1 ± 0.3 mm consistent with camera observations.

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: For deep flexion, similar refinements altered peak pressures by 2.6% and footprint posteriorization by 0.2 mm (9%).

findings.mechanism: Peak contact stress in deep flexion under axial–rotational load
findings.span: For peak contact stress in deep flexion, a quasistaticplustran-sient protocol was used: flexion of 120°, axial load stepped to 2,800 N over 25 ms, followed by a 15 ms ramp of an internal tibial rotation to 15° with a superimposed 18 N·m torque, maintaining small AP shear (<60 N).

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
findings.span: For rimloading, dyed contact revealing methods confirmed footprint position relative to the tibial insert rim.

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
findings.span: EXDKnee v1.2 emphasizes highfidelity transient contact and stress fields using explicit time integration.

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
findings.span: Edgeloading under varus malalignment produced concentrated contact at the insert rim.

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
findings.span: Rim loading was more sensitive: increasing penalty stiffness by 50% increased peak rim pressure by 4.5%, and shifting internal rotation from 5° to 6° increased rimcontact width by 7.9%.

findings.mechanism: Edge-loading under varus malalignment with internal tibial rotation
findings.span: For rim loading, the 95% interval for peak rim pressure widened to ±22% (EXDKnee v1.2), and the volumetric wear fraction at the rim varied with ±19% halfwidth (EXDWearGrow v2.0), reflecting strong amplification of small alignment and friction changes.

findings.mechanism: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
findings.span: Post–cam loads were measured via a custom instrumented cam with a uniaxial highbandwidth force transducer (10 kHz sampling), in series with highspeed video (2,000 fps) to track relative cam–post approach velocity and engagement timing; the rig delivered impacts with 0.1–0.6 J kinetic energy.

findings.mechanism: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
findings.span: Energy balance checks tracked kinetic, internal, hourglass, contact, and artificial energies; cumulative artificial energy remained below 0.5% of the sum of kinetic and internal energies during level walking, 0.9% during deep flexion, 1.1% during rim loading, and 0.8% during post–cam impacts.

findings.mechanism: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
findings.span: For post–cam impacts during stair descent, EXDKnee v1.2 reproduced instrumented cam peak forces of 950 ± 110 N with predicted 880–1,010 N across timing variations (7.4% median deviation).

findings.mechanism: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
findings.span: For post–cam engagement, halving the time step shifted peak cam force by 1.9% and engagement timing by 0.4 ms.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: External data included two peerreviewed simulator studies reporting PS knee wear rates under ISO conditions with sufficient metadata to reconstruct boundary conditions and surface finishes.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: The wear–creep growth loop in EXDWearGrow v2.0 was exercised on canonical problems with known solutions: for a flatonflat crawler under uniform pressure, the accumulated wear depth over 1 Mc matched the Archard solution to within 1.9%; a wedge indentation creep test reproduced the Findley prediction to within 3.5% after 10,000 s equivalent time.

findings.mechanism: Articular surface wear during level walking (ISO-style input profiles)
findings.span: EXDWearGrow v2.0 predicted volumetric wear over 5 Mc of 172 ± 19 mm3, or 34.4 ± 3.8 mm3/Mc, compared with inhouse simulator 36.8 ± 5.2 mm3/Mc (6.5%) and literature means 33 ± 6 mm3/Mc (+4.2%) and 41 ± 9 mm3/Mc (16.1%).

findings.mechanism: Post–cam impact and sliding during stair descent and sit-to-stand
findings.span: Material and friction perturbations (±10% Einst, ±10% yield, µ in 0.03–0.08) changed gait pressures by ≤4.1% and wear by ≤6.7% (driven largely by µ and k coupling into crossshear), deepflexion peak pressures by ≤8.9%, rimloading peaks by ≤11.0%, and peak cam forces by ≤5.4%.
